top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) is a distinct architecture from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, is reproduced near 1e-18 across laboratories and species, and has separable, uncontested credit for Katori (concept, first Sr lattice clock) and Ye (accuracy frontier). It is a measurement capability rather than a new phenomenon, but the maturity and clean two-name allocation make an award preferable to none, provided the citation is worded around the lattice concept.
